top_story.headline: Marshals Service gives Coinbase an $8.1 million no-bid cryptocurrency custody contract after a reported $46 million theft at its previous contractor
top_story.dek: The U.S. Marshals Service says it faces an urgent risk to seized crypto and that Coinbase is the only company that already holds its required security authorization.
paragraphs: The U.S. Marshals Service (Department of Justice) plans to award Coinbase Inc. an 18-month contract for custody, management and disposal of seized cryptocurrency, with no competition. The justification puts the estimated value at $8,128,125. It invokes unusual and compelling urgency, citing "an emergent and urgent situation that requires an immediate solution in order to avoid further possible loss of seized cryptocurrency" (notice, justification).

The justification says Coinbase "is the only company with a current Authorization to Use (ATU) designation, required by the USMS who could perform work without substantial interruption." It also says the earlier Class 2-4 award went to Command Services and Support Inc. and "was unsuccessfully protested by an unsuccessful offeror at the Agency level and the GAO." Separately, the document describes a stop-work notice issued January 23, 2026 after an employee of that incumbent allegedly stole seized cryptocurrency, a loss it puts at at least $46 million. That passage was not independently matched word for word against the file, so it is reported here as the document's own account.
USAspending shows a Coinbase federal contract on record since May 2020, so this is not its first government work. The resulting vehicle is a commercial firm-fixed-price indefinite-delivery contract.

sections.headline: NASA skips competition twice for Artemis, citing Executive Order 14369 and a race with China
paragraphs: There are 24 new justifications, 14 of them posted under other notice types such as Award Notices and Special Notices, and 9 repeats from earlier editions were left out. The Marshals Service cryptocurrency deal is today's Top Story and four bridges and extensions are in the Extensions section below.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: NASA adds spacesuit hardware production to Axiom Space's lunar suit contract without competition, citing an executive order
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: NASA's Johnson Space Center wants to add a hardware production and delivery line (CLIN 5) to contract 80JSC022DA022, running through May 30, 2032. Because xEVAS is a services contract, the document says an approved justification is needed to add a supply line on a sole-source basis. It cites Executive Order 14369, "Ensuring American Space Superiority" (return to the Moon by 2028), but says the order "is cited to document the schedule context only." The document says two xEVAS contracts were awarded on May 31, 2022, to Axiom Space and Collins Aerospace. USAspending shows an Axiom federal contract on record since 2018.

blocks.title: NASA buys Artemis rocket avionics from Space Vector without competition, citing urgency and the race with China
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
blocks.text: NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center is buying Secondary Payload Avionics Units and engineering support, including a spare, for the Artemis IV and V missions of the Space Launch System. The justification says it is "critical to the national interests of the United States" that Artemis "return American astronauts to the Moon before China reaches this milestone." It also cites Executive Order 14369 and says Space Vector LLC designed the units that already flew on Artemis I and Artemis II.

blocks.title: Air Force keeps KBR Wyle running Wright-Patterson's centrifuge and altitude chambers without competition
meta: value redacted in justification, award record lists $15,000,000
only one company can do it
blocks.text: Posted as an Award Notice, this is a 60-month indefinite-delivery contract to operate and maintain the Centrifuge and Research Altitude Chambers at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, for the 711th Human Performance Wing. The justification says the contract "must be awarded and fully operational by the start of Fiscal Year 2027 (1 October 2026)." The award record is dated September 25, 2026. The agency says KBR Wyle Services, LLC, the incumbent, "has been the only company in this operational and research area to recruit retired and separated military Aerospace Physiology specialists."

blocks.text: Washington Headquarters Services is buying Executive Champion Orientation training for the Office of the Secretary of War, built on the proprietary Danaher Business System methodology. The justification says only Pall Aeropower, as a Danaher subsidiary, has access to the curriculum and authorized instructional materials. sections.headline: General Services Administration gives Marine Corps logistics team a $92.6 million no-competition bridge while its replacement is competed
paragraphs: Four new justifications keep an incumbent running. Two are large enough for cards and two are listed below.

blocks.title: General Services Administration gives Marine Corps logistics team a $92.6 million no-competition bridge while its replacement is competed
meta: MSC Industrial Direct CO., Inc., L C Industries, Inc. and OSC Solutions, Inc.
skipped the competition among existing contract holders (logical follow-on)
blocks.text: General Services Administration is issuing a 3-month purchase agreement, with one 3-month option, to the team behind the current Marine Corps 4PL NextGen I supply chain agreements, valued at $950,356,271 and extended to January 25, 2027. The bridge covers Marine Corps locations in the continental U.S., Hawaii and Japan while the agency competes the NextGen II request for quotations (47QSCC26Q5001), issued June 15, 2026. The justification calls the order a "logical follow-on to an FSS order already issued on a competitive basis." It says transition timelines and Status of Forces Agreement certification abroad prevent a new contractor from starting in time.

blocks.title: Air Force extends RC-135 aircrew training contract another six months without competition after the recompete slipped to 2027
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: Air Combat Command will extend contract FA4890-21-C-0001 for RC-135 aircrew training and courseware at Offutt Air Force Base, Nebraska, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027. The Air Force already used a clause (52.217-8) on April 1, 2026 to run services through October 31, 2026. It blames the "October - November 2025 Government shutdown and requirement changes due to DOGE feedback" for delaying the recompete, with award now anticipated February 1, 2027. The original contract was a service-disabled veteran-owned small business set-aside awarded February 4, 2021.

sections.headline: Defense Logistics Agency awards five 10-year military medical supply contracts worth up to $21.5 billion
paragraphs: Of 326 new award notices, 27 were flagged and 48 repeats were left out. The medical supply batch and two Navy phone awards are written up below.

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency picks Cardinal Health, McKesson and Concordance for 10-year military medical supply contracts worth up to $21.5 billion
meta: Cardinal Health 200, LLC, McKesson Medical-Surgical Government Solutions LLC, Concordance Healthcare Solutions LLC
blocks.text: The Defense Logistics Agency awarded five Medical Surgical Prime Vendor contracts on October 27, 2026. Cardinal Health 200, LLC won the North primary (up to $8.84 billion) and West primary (up to $6.57 billion), McKesson Medical-Surgical Government Solutions LLC the South primary (up to $4.37 billion), and Concordance Healthcare Solutions LLC the North back-up ($982 million) and West back-up ($730 million). Each is a fixed-price indefinite-delivery contract with a 30-month base and three 30-month options, ending June 6, 2037. They serve the Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps, with the Defense Health Agency, Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Health and Human Services as additional customers.

sections.headline: Defense Logistics Agency Energy and the Army plan to hand Hawaii's Army water system to a private owner

blocks.title: Defense Logistics Agency Energy and the Army plan to hand Hawaii's Army water system to a private owner
blocks.text: Defense Logistics Agency Energy, working with the Army, plans to privatize the water distribution system at U.S. Army Garrison-Hawaii on Oahu. Under 10 U.S.C. §2688, the selected contractor would "assume ownership of the Water utility system" and take over operations, maintenance, repair and future upgrades and replacements. Six of 23 attachments are access-restricted and 17 are queued to be read in later editions.
